newsitem.title: USA: Suspected ex-Nazi guard dies in Kansas hospital.
newsitem.headline: Suspected ex-Nazi guard dies in Kansas hospital.

text.p: A suspected former Nazi concentration camp guard died in the hospital where he had been staying since being involved in a shootout with police, a hospital spokesman said on Monday.
Michael Kolnhofer, a resident of Kansas City, Kansas, died shortly before midnight on Sunday, a spokesman at the University of Kansas Medical Centre said.
The spokesman declined to comment on the cause of death, but local media reports said Kolnhofer died of an aneurysm.
Kolnhofer was taken to the hospital on Dec. 31 after police shot him outside his home. A bullet passed through both of his legs, and doctors said he may have suffered brain damage during surgery.

Kolnhofer, accused of having committed wartime atrocities, had fired at police and journalists in a confrontation that began after the Justice Department said it was seeking to revoke his citizenship because of alleged wartime crimes.

The Justice Department's Nazi-hunting Office of Special Investigations said Kolnhofer, who was born in Croatia when it was part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, had concealed his identity when he emigrated to the United States in 1952.
At the time, Kolnhofer said he had served in the German army on the Russian front during the Second World War.
